title: Affine inert refinements of equivariant pointed etale neighbourhoods
statement:
Let $G$ be a finite group acting by scheme automorphisms on a separated locally Noetherian scheme $X$ [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-proper-morphism, pqf-def-locnoeth]. Let $\bar x:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X$ be a geometric point [def-weil-geometric-point], and put $H=\{g\in G:g\bar x=\bar x\}$. Let $f:V\to X$ be an $H$-equivariant etale morphism [def-weil-etale-morphism] from a scheme with an $H$-action, where $H$ acts on $X$ by inclusion in $G$, and let $\bar v$ be an $H$-fixed geometric point of $V$ with $f\bar v=\bar x$. For any $H$-invariant open subscheme $O\subseteq V$ containing $\bar v$, there exist an affine Noetherian scheme $W$ with an $H$-action, an $H$-fixed geometric point $\bar w$, and an $H$-equivariant etale morphism $a:W\to V$ factoring through $O$, such that $a\bar w=\bar v$ and, for every geometric point $\bar z$ of $W$, inclusion of groups identifies
$$\operatorname{Stab}_H(\bar z)=\operatorname{Stab}_G(fa\bar z).$$
A scheme action here means automorphisms $a_g$ satisfying $a_1=1$ and $a_{gh}=a_ga_h$; equivariance means commutation with these automorphisms. A geometric stabilizer consists of elements fixing the geometric-point morphism, including its residue-field embedding. No log structure, tameness, regularity, quotient existence or faithful action is assumed.

source.place: VIII 5.3.6 and the initial localization argument of proof 5.3.7, printed p.124; VI 4.1, p.76, fixed subschemes. Generic affine equivariant refinement underlying the inert shrinking, before any rigidification. In ancestor lem-per-artin-gabber-affine-curve this serves proof Step 3, regular local model and purity.

proof.text: For $g\in G$, form the equalizer $F_g=X\times_{X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}X,(1,g),\Delta_X}X$. By [def-weil-proper-morphism] the diagonal is a closed immersion; [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change] therefore makes $F_g\hookrightarrow X$ a closed immersion. Its universal property says that a geometric point $\bar y$ factors through it exactly when $g\bar y=\bar y$. Put $X_0=X\setminus\bigcup_{g\notin H}|F_g|$. This is open, contains $\bar x$, and every geometric point in it has $G$-stabilizer contained in $H$. For $h\in H$ the identity $hF_g=F_{hgh^{-1}}$ follows by composing the defining equality with $h$ and $h^{-1}$. Since conjugation by $H$ preserves $G\setminus H$, $X_0$ is $H$-invariant.

source.place: VI 4.1, printed p.76, fixed subschemes; VIII proof 5.3.7, printed p.124, the open X prime obtained by removing fixed loci

proof.text: Fix $h\in H$. Let $P_h=V\times_XF_h$ with inclusion $i_h:P_h\to V$, a closed immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change]. Equivariance and the equality defining $F_h$ give $fi_h=fh i_h$, so $(i_h,h i_h)$ is a map $P_h\to V\times_XV$. Pull back $\Delta_f:V\to V\times_XV$ along this map and call the resulting equalizer $E_h\to P_h$. The map $f$ is unramified by [def-weil-etale-morphism], hence its diagonal is open by [def-weil-unramified-morphism]; [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change] makes $E_h$ open in $P_h$. Thus $B_h=|P_h|\setminus|E_h|$ is closed in $P_h$, and therefore in $V$. For a geometric point $\bar z$ of $V$, membership in $P_h$ means $hf\bar z=f\bar z$, and membership in $E_h$ means also $h\bar z=\bar z$. These are equalities of morphisms, not just of their image points. In using the first equivalence, a field-valued morphism whose image is in a closed subscheme factors through it: every element of its defining ideal maps to zero in the field.

source.place: Tag 02GE, lemma-diagonal-unramified-morphism; Tag 01QR, lemma-base-change-closed-immersion; with schemes.tex Tag 01JY, lemma-base-change-immersion (open case). Explicit equalizer pullback argument

proof.text: Put $T=O\cap f^{-1}(X_0)\cap\bigl(V\setminus\bigcup_{h\in H}B_h\bigr)$. This is an open neighbourhood of $\bar v$: its image lies in $X_0$, and $h\bar v=\bar v$ puts $\bar v$ in every $E_h$. For $k\in H$, equivariance sends $P_h$ to $P_{khk^{-1}}$ and sends the equality $h\bar z=\bar z$ to $(khk^{-1})(k\bar z)=k\bar z$, so it sends $B_h$ to $B_{khk^{-1}}$. Thus $T$ is $H$-invariant. If $g\in G$ fixes $f\bar z$ for a geometric point of $T$, step 1 gives $g\in H$; then $\bar z\in P_g$ and exclusion of $B_g$ gives $\bar z\in E_g$, hence $g\bar z=\bar z$. Conversely equivariance sends every element fixing $\bar z$ to an element fixing $f\bar z$. Therefore the two stabilizers are equal on $T$.

source.place: VIII 5.3.6 and initial localization of proof 5.3.7, printed p.124; explicit elementary assembly of the fixed-locus calculations in steps 1 and 2

proof.text: Write $v$ for the image point of $\bar v$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis], choose an affine open $A$ with $v\in A\subseteq T$. Set $T_1=\bigcap_{h\in H}hA$. All its terms contain $v$, and left multiplication permutes them, so $T_1$ is an invariant open neighbourhood of $v$ contained in $A$. The scheme $A$ is separated over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-source-morphism-separated]. The diagonal of its open subscheme $T_1$ is the pullback of $\Delta_A$ along $T_1\times T_1\to A\times A$: equality of the two maps to $A$ is equality to $T_1$ because the inclusion is a monomorphism. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change] shows $T_1$ is separated. This does not assert that $T_1$ is affine.

source.place: Tags 01IT (lemma-basis-affine-opens), 01KN (lemma-affine-separated); morphisms.tex Tag 01QR. First shrinking in the explicit invariant-affine argument underlying ILO VIII proof 5.3.7

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis] again inside $T_1$, obtaining an affine open $C$ containing $v$. Put $W=\bigcap_{h\in H}hC$. The translates $hC$ are affine opens of the separated scheme $T_1$. Repeated application of [lem-weil-pbc-separated-affine-open-intersection], with base $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$, shows that their finite nonempty intersection is affine: start with $C$ and intersect the remaining translates one at a time. Each intermediate intersection is affine by that lemma. The set $W$ contains $v$, is $H$-invariant by reindexing, and is contained in $T_1\subseteq T\subseteq O$. This second shrinking is essential because $V$ itself need not be separated.

source.place: Tags 01IT (lemma-basis-affine-opens), 01KP (lemma-characterize-separated, (1)(a)); explicit finite-intersection realization of the invariant affine neighbourhoods in ILO VIII proof 5.3.7

proof.text: Restrict the $H$-action to $W$ and let $a:W\hookrightarrow V$ be the inclusion. The action laws restrict, and $a$ is equivariant and factors through $O$. Since $v\in W$, the geometric point $\bar v$ has a unique factorization $\bar w$ through $W$. For $h\in H$ the maps $h\bar w$ and $\bar w$ have the same composite $\bar v$ with the open immersion, hence agree. Thus $\bar w$ is $H$-fixed and $a\bar w=\bar v$. The map $a$ is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale]. For any geometric $\bar z$ of $W$, injectivity of an open immersion on morphisms identifies its stabilizer with that of $a\bar z$ in $T$; step 3 gives the required equality with $\operatorname{Stab}_G(fa\bar z)$.

source.place: Tag 02GP (lemma-open-immersion-etale); elementary restriction of the action and the stabilizer equality already proved

proof.text: The unramified hypothesis on $f$ makes it locally of finite type by [def-weil-unramified-morphism]. Since $X$ is locally Noetherian, [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft] makes $V$ locally Noetherian. Now $W$ is an affine open of $V$, so [pqf-lem-affine-open-locnoeth] makes its coordinate ring Noetherian. Consequently $W$ is an affine Noetherian scheme, as asserted.

proof_origin.place: VI 4.1, printed p.76 and VIII 5.3.6--5.3.7, printed p.124. Explicit general-scheme proof of the preliminary inert localization and invariant-affine shrinking; no logarithmic or tameness argument.

lean.statement: theorem exists_affine_inert_equivariant_refinement {G : Type v} [Group G] [Finite G] {X : Scheme.{u}} [X.IsSeparated] [IsLocallyNoetherian X] (ρX : G →* Aut X) {Ω : Type u} [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω] (x : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ X) (H : Subgroup G) (hH : ∀ g : G, g ∈ H ↔ x ≫ (ρX g).hom = x) {V : Scheme.{u}} (ρV : H →* Aut V) (f : V ⟶ X) [Etale f] (hf : ∀ h : H, (ρV h).hom ≫ f = f ≫ (ρX h.val).hom) (t : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ V) (ht : t ≫ f = x) (ht_fixed : ∀ h : H, t ≫ (ρV h).hom = t) (O : V.Opens) (htO : t default ∈ O) (hO : ∀ (h : H) (p : V), (ρV h).hom p ∈ O ↔ p ∈ O) : ∃ (W : Scheme.{u}) (_ : IsAffine W) (_ : IsNoetherian W) (ρW : H →* Aut W) (w : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ W) (a : W ⟶ V), Etale a ∧ (∀ h : H, (ρW h).hom ≫ a = a ≫ (ρV h).hom) ∧ (∃ b : W ⟶ O.toScheme, b ≫ O.ι = a) ∧ w ≫ a = t ∧ (∀ h : H, w ≫ (ρW h).hom = w) ∧ ∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] [IsAlgClosed K] (z : Spec (.of K) ⟶ W) (g : G), z ≫ a ≫ f ≫ (ρX g).hom = z ≫ a ≫ f ↔ ∃ h : H, h.val = g ∧ z ≫ (ρW h).hom = z
